label: tp-rules-probe
_why: PROBE (user, 2026-10-19: "Go on with the probes once run3 ends"), FINDINGS F244 §6-§7. The engine trigger is_potential_treaty_port admits only states holding a port building, and on cession the engine seeds a level-1 port in the new treaty port. Two questions: (1) can a state WITHOUT a port be made a treaty port at all, by the engine's own cession effect, by a scripted treaty, and by a treaty-port diplomatic play; (2) does replacing is_potential_treaty_port in the article and the war goal with our own candidate check (and removing the war goal's validate_take_treaty_port setting) open those routes. At the campaign start each arm runs: cede_treaty_port of Sonora (MEX, no port) and Veracruz (MEX, port) to Britain; create_treaty with a treaty-port article for Yucatan (MEX, no port) and Bahia (BRZ, port) to France; create_diplomatic_play dp_take_treaty_port by Britain on Ceara (BRZ, no port), by the USA on Rio de Janeiro (BRZ, port), by France on Fez (MOR, port). Monthly PMR_TPR lines list every treaty port Britain, France and the USA hold and whether it has a port building; monthly autosaves give the plays' war goals (save summary v19).

_arms.tpr0: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.jex-dam4s-rs-x25-m10ac-dpriv-wm99-tpr0.json} - the next-arm base (canon + monopoly threshold 0.99) + the probe effects; vanilla treaty-port rules

_comparison: tpr1 against tpr0, test by test; the port-holding controls (Veracruz, Bahia, Rio de Janeiro, Fez) must succeed in both or the test itself is broken.

_predictions.cede: Veracruz becomes a British treaty port in both arms; Sonora UNKNOWN - the effect is engine code (if it refuses a portless state, no script change can remove the requirement)
_predictions.treaty: Bahia becomes a French treaty port in both arms; Yucatan fails in tpr0 (the article's state_valid_trigger) and succeeds in tpr1 if the engine accepts the cession
_predictions.play: the Rio de Janeiro and Fez plays exist in both arms; the Ceara play is refused in tpr0 and exists in tpr1 unless the engine's own war-goal validation still applies (or Britain lacks an interest there - then the Rio de Janeiro control tells the interest apart only if it shares the region, which it does)

_cost: 2 runs x 1836.1.1 -> 1836.7.1 with monthly autosaves, about 8 min each
_caveats: Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (L30).
Probe effects at the campaign start change six states' ownership and start three plays: never a book to play.
